Help me to build a website that will be used as a resource to coach professionals on how to integrate AI in the workplace. I would like the site to feel very professional and polished, but in a welcoming way that doesn't feel like another tech-company website. Dark mode themes should be used, prioritizing white text on black or grey backgrounds, mainly using Product Sans as the main font, alternating the amount of bold between titles and body texts. I would like to make the different sections on the website "glow" when the mouse hovers over, and then a simple but unique animation when a button is pressed. These supporting colors can be in an aurora borealis color scheme, prioritizing vivid blues and purple hues with soft green and white interweaving. It should feel very modern, almost mimicking the Google Gemini color scheme and polished iconography. 

I would like there to also be a side menu to navigate to specific areas to learn more about AI. Users will have to click on these side tabs to access the pages, they won't be able to just scroll down to go from page to page, however I would like the infinity scroll feeling where it makes sense. The separate pages will be "AI in action," which will be demo videos with short descriptions explaining what's happening and how to reproduce, "My recommended AI tools" based on specific needs and use cases, and a "Who i am" page which will include an overview of my background and what my goals are with this online AI coaching resource.

My focus has shifted to the application's core architecture. I've decided to implement state-based routing instead of React Router to streamline navigation. Now I'm breaking down content: the homepage will include an intro and an "Ask AI" chat. The "AI in Action" page will dynamically query Gemini for the latest AI use cases. The "Recommended Tools" section will incorporate a filterable list driven by Gemini's recommendations. Finally, a straightforward bio page will wrap it all up.


**Implementing Page Structure**

I'm now focusing on "AI in Action" page functionality. I've decided to let users request a new "demo idea" if the current example isn't what they're looking for. The next step is fleshing out the application's step-by-step implementation, including the setup of `metadata.json`, `index.html`, `index.tsx`, and `types.ts`. I plan to integrate `lucide-react` for icons and set up the Gemini client within `services/gemini.ts` for tool recommendations and chat responses. **Outlining Page Components**

I'm solidifying the page components: `Home.tsx` will be a welcome page with a quick chat feature.  `AIInAction.tsx` will have video placeholders. A form powered by Gemini for tool suggestions will be in `Tools.tsx`, and `Bio.tsx` will host the user's profile. I'm focusing on the main layout and routing logic in `App.tsx` now.



**Developing Application Components**

I'm now diving into the component implementation. I'm starting with `types.ts` and `services/geminiService.ts`, followed by `components/Sidebar.tsx`, `components/GlowCard.tsx`, and `components/Button.tsx` which will feature an animation. I've set up the basic structure for the "Recommended Tools" view, with an input field and button to connect with the `geminiService` and show `GlowCard` results.
